cleanIntro: The FLOW 9 M is a modular titanium can, and HUXWRX's own product manual covers it. It ships in its short configuration: the suppressor body with the module adapter thread protector on the front, and a booster assembly (booster piston, booster spring, piston adapter and piston O-ring) at the rear with a 1/2x28 piston. The FLOW 9 M Module in the box screws onto the front in place of the thread protector to make it long. HUXWRX's book sets two cycles: the booster assembly cleaned after every session of shooting, and the suppressor itself cleaned every 1,000 to 2,000 rounds. The included pistol wrench does the work on the booster and the barrel. The book prints no cartridge rating for the can: the rating marked on your can is the limit.

steps.title: Clear the host before the can is touched
steps.action: Unload the host firearm before either end of the can is handled: magazine out, chamber empty, and checked by eye. HUXWRX puts this warning first in its book and repeats it at the head of both the installation and the accessory sections, so it applies whether the can is coming off or going on. The host's own manual is the authority on how its action is cleared.
steps.prose: Every removal on this can is wrench work directly in front of the muzzle.
steps.quote: Firearm may be loaded. Could result in death or serious injury. Ensure the firearm is unloaded.
steps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — WARNINGS & DEFINITIONS, p.2
steps.warn: Unloaded and checked before a wrench goes near the muzzle.

steps.title: Let it cool, and wear gloves
steps.action: After firing, the suppressor can be hot enough to cause serious burns. Let it cool, and wear protective gloves when you handle it, as HUXWRX asks. Set it down where it cannot burn or melt anything while it cools.
steps.prose: The gloves also matter for the cleaning that follows: the book warns of lead exposure.
steps.quote: Allow the suppressor to cool and wear protective gloves.
steps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — WARNINGS & DEFINITIONS, p.2
steps.warn: Hot cans burn. Wait, and wear gloves.

steps.title: The right ammunition, and a thread that matches
steps.action: HUXWRX warns that ammunition of the wrong caliber for the suppressor may still fit the firearm, and that firing it can kill or seriously injure. The book prints no cartridge rating for the FLOW 9 M, so the rating marked on your can is the limit. Its installation check is that the barrel and the accessory thread pattern match: the can ships with a 1/2x28 piston. If you are not certain of your can's rating, ask HUXWRX Support before you fire it.
steps.prose: Know the caliber and the thread before it goes on a gun.
steps.quote: Ensure correct caliber of ammunition for suppressor is being used.
steps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — WARNINGS & DEFINITIONS, p.2
steps.warn: Caliber and thread pattern both match, or it does not go on.

steps.title: The booster is for a recoiling barrel
steps.action: The FLOW 9 M ships with its booster assembly fitted and greased. HUXWRX says the booster with its spring is what lets the can work on a host whose barrel moves to cycle, such as a tilting-barrel pistol. The book lists direct thread, stiction and 3-lug adapters and a fixed barrel spacer as accessories; to use any of them the booster assembly comes out and the threads are cleaned first. Know which mount is in your can before it goes on a gun.
steps.prose: A recoiling-barrel pistol needs the booster with its spring.
steps.quote: The booster assembly with spring is necessary to function on weapon systems where the barrel reciprocates to cycle.
steps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — ACCESSORY INSTALLATION & REMOVAL, item 1, p.6
steps.warn: Booster with spring on a barrel that reciprocates.

steps.title: Off the host with the pistol wrench
steps.action: If the host is a handgun, lock the slide open first, as the book does to make room for the pistol wrench with a torque wrench on it. The can went on by tightening the piston to the barrel with the included pistol wrench, to 15 to 25 ft-lb, so it comes off the same way: the pistol wrench on the piston, turned to unscrew it from the barrel. Expect it to need the tool rather than a hand on the tube.
steps.prose: The book prints the installation; removal is the same tool on the same part, turned the other way.
steps.quote: For handguns, lock the slide open to allow more room for the pistol Wrench with torque wrench attached.
steps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — SUPPRESSOR INSTALLATION, item 1, p.5
steps.warn: The wrench goes on the piston, not the tube.

steps.title: Booster assembly out of the housing
steps.action: Put the pistol wrench on the piston base flats and, if it needs an opposing force, an adjustable wrench on the piston flats, then unscrew the booster assembly from the housing. This is the first step of HUXWRX's every-session cleaning. Lay out the booster piston, the booster spring, the piston adapter and the piston O-ring where none of them can roll away. The front of the can stays as it is until the Deep Clean.
steps.prose: If a joint will not break free with the wrenches where the book puts them, stop and contact HUXWRX Support rather than adding force.
steps.quote: To disassemble the booster assembly from the housing, use the pistol wrench on the piston base flats along with an adjustable wrench on the piston flats if necessary.
steps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — ACCESSORY INSTALLATION & REMOVAL, item 3, p.6
steps.warn: Wrenches on the flats the book names. No extra force.

steps.title: CLP, then wipe every piece clean
steps.action: Apply CLP or a similar cleaner to the booster parts, then wipe each piece with a lint-free rag until the debris and carbon are gone. HUXWRX asks for this after every session of shooting, so it belongs to every range trip, not to the Deep Clean. Wear gloves: the book warns of lead exposure.
steps.prose: Lint-free, as the book says: fibres left on the piston end up in the joint.
steps.quote: Wipe all individual pieces with a lint-free rag, removing all debris and carbon.
steps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — RECOMMENDED CLEANING CYCLE, item 3, p.7

steps.title: Check the O-ring
steps.action: Look at the piston O-ring for cracking or wear each time the booster is out. HUXWRX sells a Piston O-ring kit as a replacement part, PN 2584, so a worn O-ring is replaced rather than put back.
steps.prose: The replacement part numbers are in the book's parts list.
steps.quote: Inspect o-ring for cracking or wear.
steps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — RECOMMENDED CLEANING CYCLE, item 4, p.7

steps.title: Grease every face
steps.action: Apply Ceram-X or another high-temperature grease to all faces of the booster parts: the piston, the spring and the O-ring, and the contact points between the muzzle device and the suppressor. HUXWRX ships the booster greased and asks for grease on it before use.
steps.prose: High-temperature grease, as the book specifies.
steps.quote: Apply Ceram-X or other high-temp grease to all faces.
steps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — RECOMMENDED CLEANING CYCLE, item 5, p.7

steps.title: Barrel and threads inspected and clean
steps.action: Look over the host barrel and its threads for debris and any sign of damage, and clean every thread you are about to put back together: the barrel's, the piston's and the housing's. HUXWRX asks for clean threads before every assembly it describes. A damaged thread is a reason not to mount the can.
steps.prose: Clean threads are what let the can seat and torque as the book intends.
steps.quote: Inspect barrel and threads for debris and any signs of damage/defect.
steps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — ACCESSORY INSTALLATION & REMOVAL, p.6

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The can is off the host and the booster assembly is out, cleaned, checked and greased. The suppressor body, the thread protector or the module stay as they are for this clean: HUXWRX's cycle for cleaning the suppressor itself is every 1,000 to 2,000 rounds, which is the Deep Clean.
steps.prose: Reassembly for this path is the booster back in and the can back on the host.
steps.quote: Clean the booster assembly after each session of shooting
steps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — RECOMMENDED CLEANING CYCLE, p.7

deepSteps.title: Front piece off the body
deepSteps.action: With the can off the host and the booster out, unscrew whatever is on the front of the suppressor body: the module adapter thread protector in the short configuration, or the extension module in the long one. HUXWRX notes that an adjustable wrench on the piston flats can be used as the opposing force. Both go on by hand, so they should come off with the same.
deepSteps.prose: This is the same operation the book uses to change the can's length.
deepSteps.quote: An adjustable wrench on the piston flats can be used as an opposing force to remove the extension module and piston base.
deepSteps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — SUPPRESSOR ASSEMBLY, p.5

deepSteps.title: This is as far as it comes apart
deepSteps.action: The book's teardown ends here: the front piece off the body and the booster assembly out of the housing. HUXWRX publishes no procedure for taking the suppressor body itself apart, and its warning page says not to modify components, because incorrect or modified components can kill or seriously injure. The body is cleaned as it is.
deepSteps.prose: Anything past this is a question for HUXWRX Support, not for the bench.
deepSteps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — WARNINGS & DEFINITIONS, p.2
deepSteps.warn: Nothing past the front piece and the booster.

deepSteps.title: Clean the suppressor every 1,000 to 2,000 rounds
deepSteps.action: Every 1,000 to 2,000 rounds, clean the suppressor itself. HUXWRX names its own Suppressor Sauce as the preferred cleaning solution for its suppressors; use the solution as its own instructions direct. This book gives no soak time and no other method, so it is quoted here and nothing is added to it.
deepSteps.prose: Get every thread clean before anything goes back on.
deepSteps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — RECOMMENDED CLEANING CYCLE, p.7

deepSteps.title: Gloves, eye protection, a respirator, and air
deepSteps.action: Wear gloves, eye protection and a respiratory mask while you clean, and work where the air moves. HUXWRX warns that cleaning exposes you to lead, and asks you to wash your hands thoroughly afterwards.
deepSteps.prose: The lead warning is on the book's warning page as well as its cleaning page.
deepSteps.quote: Utilize proper PPE (i.e. Gloves, eye protection, and respiratory mask)
deepSteps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — RECOMMENDED CLEANING CYCLE, p.7

deepSteps.title: Dispose of used solution properly
deepSteps.action: Used cleaning solution carries lead and fouling. Dispose of it the way your local guidelines require, as HUXWRX asks; it does not go down a drain by default.
deepSteps.prose: Check your local rules before you pour anything away.
deepSteps.quote: Please refer to your local guidelines for proper disposal procedures of used cleaning solutions.
deepSteps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — RECOMMENDED CLEANING CYCLE, p.7

deepSteps.title: Front piece back on by hand
deepSteps.action: With the threads clean, thread the front piece back onto the front of the suppressor body by hand until it seats: the extension module for the long configuration, or the module adapter thread protector for the short one. The book has both go on by hand.
deepSteps.prose: Clean threads first, as the book asks before every assembly.
deepSteps.quote: Thread the extension module onto the front of the suppressor body by hand until seated.
deepSteps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — SUPPRESSOR ASSEMBLY, item 3, p.5

deepSteps.title: Booster back in, torqued to specification
deepSteps.action: Grease the piston, spring and O-ring with Ceram-X or another high-temperature grease, refit the booster assembly to the housing, and torque it to specification: the book's chart gives the piston adapter to the suppressor at 100 to 115 in-lb. HUXWRX asks for the piston assembly to be firmly torqued before firing.
deepSteps.prose: The torque figures are in the book's accessory torque chart.
deepSteps.cite: FLOW 9 M PRODUCT MANUAL — RECOMMENDED CLEANING CYCLE, item 6, p.7

cleaning.name: BOOSTER ASSEMBLY — EVERY SESSION
tasks: Booster assembly out of the housing: pistol wrench on the piston base flats, an adjustable wrench on the piston flats if needed
CLP or a similar cleaner, then every piece wiped with a lint-free rag until the debris and carbon are gone
The O-ring checked for cracking or wear; a worn one replaced (Piston O-ring kit, PN 2584)
Ceram-X or another high-temperature grease on all faces

cleaning.name: THREADS & BARREL
tasks: Barrel and threads inspected for debris and any sign of damage
Every thread clean before assembly: barrel, piston, housing and the front of the body

cleaning.name: SUPPRESSOR — EVERY 1,000 TO 2,000 ROUNDS
tasks: This group is the Deep Clean: the front piece comes off the body
Suppressor Sauce is HUXWRX's preferred cleaning solution; use it as its own instructions direct
Do not modify components: the body is cleaned as it is, never taken apart

cleaning.name: WHILE YOU CLEAN
tasks: Gloves, eye protection and a respiratory mask
A well-ventilated area, and hands washed thoroughly afterwards: cleaning exposes you to lead
Used cleaning solution disposed of as your local guidelines require

reassembly: Clean every thread before assembly: the front of the body, the housing, the piston and the host barrel.
Thread the extension module (long configuration) or the module adapter thread protector (short configuration) onto the front of the suppressor body by hand until seated.
Grease the piston, spring and O-ring with Ceram-X or another high-temperature grease, refit the booster assembly to the housing, and torque the piston adapter to the suppressor at 100 to 115 in-lb.

Handgun host: lock the slide open. Check the barrel and the piston share a thread pattern, thread the can on until it bottoms out on the crown or shoulder of the barrel, and tighten the piston to the barrel with the pistol wrench, firmly by hand or with a 1/2-inch drive torque wrench to 15 to 25 ft-lb.
Check bore alignment with an alignment rod before firing.
fncheck: Before the first shot, confirm the piston assembly is firmly torqued, which HUXWRX requires before firing, that the front piece is seated by hand on the body, and that the can bottomed out on the barrel's crown or shoulder and was tightened on the piston with the pistol wrench. Run an alignment rod through to confirm the can is aligned to the bore. On a recoiling-barrel pistol the booster assembly with its spring must be the mount fitted.
reassemblyRoutine: Clean the threads, grease the piston, spring and O-ring with Ceram-X or another high-temperature grease, refit the booster assembly to the housing, and torque the piston adapter to the suppressor at 100 to 115 in-lb.

Handgun host: lock the slide open. Check the barrel and the piston share a thread pattern, thread the can on until it bottoms out on the crown or shoulder of the barrel, and tighten the piston to the barrel with the pistol wrench, firmly by hand or with a 1/2-inch drive torque wrench to 15 to 25 ft-lb.
Check bore alignment with an alignment rod before firing.

Run an alignment rod through to confirm the can is aligned to the bore. On a recoiling-barrel pistol the booster assembly with its spring must be the mount fitted.
